one_line_thesis: Warrior Met Coal is a low-leverage Alabama met coal producer rebounding from a 2025 trough.

deep_dive.executive_summary: Warrior Met Coal is a low-leverage Alabama met coal producer rebounding from a 2025 trough. At $89.61, we expect about 2.29% per year over seven years on normalized owner cash. Component proofs sum to roughly $12 per share versus price near $90, so the market may be capitalizing cycle recovery. We propose watch.

method_fit.label: Capital cycle and normalized industry economics
applicability_tests: Industry capacity, additions, closures, and replacement costs can be measured.
Current margins can be located relative to a cycle rather than extrapolated.
Maintenance and growth capital are separated.
Leverage and liquidity survive the low case.
failure_modes: replacement cost used for assets that cannot earn their cost of capital

validation_cohort.purpose: Test depletion, commodity exposure, finite reserves, and royalty-unit reconciliation.
Test tangible capital, credit losses, funding, regulation, and excess-capital realization.
Test owner earnings, capital-light reinvestment, cyclicality, and buyback value creation.
Test normalized margins, industry supply response, replacement cost, and reinvestment timing.
Test product concentration, pipeline probabilities, patent cliffs, and catalyst timing.

method_fit.rule: Use one primary method and no more than two corroborating methods; irrelevant methods and personas remain silent.

outcomes.weighting_rule: Do not change a persona's relevance within a power zone until at least 20 attributable, dividend-aware outcomes exist there; never reweight automatically.

industry.structure: Global seaborne metallurgical coal is an oligopoly of large low-cost mines plus marginal producers; pricing is spot and index-linked with high cyclicality. U.S. Gulf Coast exports compete with Australia and Canada on quality and freight.
industry.share_shift: Warrior holds premium Blue Creek-type reserves in Alabama; share gains depend on longwall uptime and port/rail access rather than greenfield discovery among U.S. peers.
industry.trend: 2025 was a pricing trough for met coal after 2022–2023 peaks; 2026 H1 rebound tracks steel demand and supply disruptions. Blue Creek development and Section 45X critical-mineral credits for met coal (OBBBA, 10-K FY2025) are current industry policy tailwinds.

Component proofs sum to roughly $12 per share versus price near $90, so the market may be capitalizing cycle recovery. We propose watch. ---
